the role of RAD18 Arg302 Gln and XPD Arg312Asn polymorphism in the risk for type-2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension and smoking, tobacco chewing and alcohol consumption in the population of Northeast India.
the identification of genetic factors that might contribute to the risk for TDM and HT in a Northeast Indian population.
the effect of polymorphism in RAD18 and XPD genes on the risk for T 2 DM and HT in association smoking, tobacco chewing and alcohol consumption.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polymorphisms in the RAD18 Arg302, XPD Asp312, APE1 Asp147 and OGG1 Cys326 genes may be considered as a potential biomarker for T2DM in association with HT.
the RAD18 Arg/Gln and XPD Asn/Gln polymorphisms in association with smoking are important independent risk factors for T2DM/HT.
RAD18 Arg/Gln and XPD Asn/Gln genotypes are associated with T2DM and/or HT risk, but only in smokers and tobacco chewers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RAD18 Arg/Gln and XPD Asn/Gln genotypes are significantly associated with T2DM and/or HT in association with tobacco chewing and/or alcohol consumption.
the risk of T2DM and/or HT increases in individuals with the RAD18 Gln and/or XPD Asn genotype in the presence of the environmental factors of smoking, tobacco chewing and/or alcohol consumption.
the risk for TDM and HT in this population was found to be associated with RAD18 Arg302 Gln (rs373572) and XPD Asp 312Asn (rs179979) polymorphisms in association with smoking.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RAD18 Arg/Gln and XPD Asn polymorphisms may be used as biomarkers for the prediction of T2DM and/or HT risk in association with smoking.
smoking is the most important independent risk for T2D and HT.
